newsitem.title: USA: Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley report higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley report higher profits.

text.p: Wall Street investment houses Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. and Morgan Stanley Group Inc. Tuesday reported strong gains in profits amid a boom in trading and mergers.
Morgan Stanley, the global leader in mergers and acquisitions, said its profits rose 26 percent, while Lehman Brothers earnings soared 84 percent.
Morgan Stanley said its profits rose to $236 million, or $1.43 a share, for its fiscal fourth quarter ended on Nov. 30, from year-earlier earnings of $187 million, or $1.08 a share.
Revenues soared to $1.51 billion from $1.17 billion.

"We have just completed a very successful year at Morgan Stanley," said Chairman Richard Fisher. "In addition to producing record earnings, we made substantial strides in our strategy of building the leading global financial services franchise."

The firm also said that its board approved the repurchase of an additional $400 million worth of common stock and a 14 percent increase in its quarterly dividend. Morgan Stanley said it bought back about $507 million of stock in fiscal 1996 and $103 million in 1995.

Morgan Stanley's profits, however, fell short of Wall Street expectations, which averaged $1.51 per share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates. The stock was off 87.50 cents at $55.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
"Morgan Stanley came in light," said Raphael Soifer, an analyst at Brown Brothers Harriman. "I think there's probably a bit of disappointment, particularly with respect to expenses."
In the fourth quarter, the firm's expenses rose to $1.15 billion from $892 million in the comparable 1995 period.

Morgan Stanley said the revenues at its investment banking unit jumped to a record $572 million, beating the old high of $542 million set in the second quarter of 1996. Revenues in the fiscal fourth quarter of 1995 totalled $503 million.
Morgan Stanley said it clinched for the second year in a row the No. 1 ranking in global mergers and acquisitions.
Revenues from sales and trading exploded to $514 million from $218 million and its asset management unit nearly doubled its revenues to $189 million from $95 million a year earlier.
The 14 percent increase in its regular quarterly dividend will bring its payout to 20 cents a share from 17.5 cents, payable on Feb. 6 to stockholders of record on Jan. 20.
Lehman Brothers said its net income rose to $127 million, or 96 cents a share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended on Nov. 30, vs. $69 million, or 49 cents a share a year earlier.
Revenues rose to $1.07 billion from $884 million.
"The fourth quarter was an excellent one for Lehman Brothers, by far the best we've had since the firm went public in 1994," said Chairman Richard Fuld Jr.

Although Lehman Brothers beat Wall Street's expectations for profits of 85 cents a share, the report was not enough to overcome general weakness in financial stocks on Tuesday. Lehman's stock was off 87.5 cents at $29.75 on the NYSE.

"Everything went right for Lehman in the quarter," Soifer said, noting its results improved despite a $50 million charge to exit the precious metals business in the United States, Europe, and Asia and to consolidate its Asian fixed income risk management activities into a single centre in Tokyo.
Lehman also said it intended to increase its dividend by 20 percent to an annual rate of 24 cents a share from 20 cents.
Lehman said that during the fourth quarter it had strong results from equity and debt underwriting and trading, foreign exchange, high yield and emerging markets.
For the year, it ranked third among global underwriters of debt and stocks, Lehman said.
Trading revenues were up 7 percent to $465 million, and investment banking revenues rose 19 percent to $310 million. Revenues from commissions fell 11 percent to $96 million.
